name: Causal Reasoning Tagging & Extraction
description: Evaluates the logical depth and structural authenticity of causal reasoning chains within a text.
mechanism: This method reconstructs the lexico-syntactic tree to identify and tag specific constructions of causation (e.g., explicit markers like 'because', 'therefore', alongside implicit verbal causatives). LLMs frequently generate plausible-sounding text where causal links are syntactically valid but logically superficial, relying on templated transitional adverbs. By analyzing the density, diversity, and structural complexity of the extracted causal arguments against empirical human baselines established by researchers like Dunietz and Girju, the algorithm flags content that over-relies on 'fake' explanatory depth.
parameters:
Analysis: Syntactic Tree Mining
Metric: Causal Link Density & Depth
Output: 0-100 Logical Homogeneity Score
accuracy: High — 78-85% on argumentative texts. Very effective at identifying the 'confident but empty' tone of AI.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Pinpointing pseudo-logical AI essays that rely heavily on transitional fluff without genuine inferential linkages.
strengths:
• Directly exposes the logical shallowness inherent in autoregressive parameter generation.
• Resistant to simple synonym replacement (spinning).
• Strongly grounded in established NLP text mining methodologies for causality.
limitations:
• Computationally expensive as it requires deep dependency parsing.
• Authentic human marketing copy or persuasive essays may be falsely flagged due to poor logical structure.
• Heavily dependent on the language's specific marker dictionary.

references.title: Dunietz, J. et al. (2017). Automatically Tagging Constructions of Causation. ACL Workshop.
Girju, R. et al. (2002). Text Mining for Causal Relations. FLAIRS Conference.
